summary: OpenAI releases API prompting and configuration guide for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models

OpenAI has published a guide for developers on how to write prompts correctly and port their projects to the next-generation language models — the flagship GPT-6.2 Astra and the cheaper GPT-6.2 Sol.
The guide describes new rules for constructing system instructions, working with caches, and abandoning some of the old generation settings.
According to the OpenAI API documentation, the flagship GPT-6.2 Astra is designed for the most complex tasks, while GPT-6.2 Sol is optimized for complex work at a lower cost.
Both models allow data storage in the US and EU, but the fastest processing mode, Ultrafast, currently only works on US servers.
Starting with the GPT-6.2 line, the Responses API has changed the rules for working with the model’s reasoning history.
If a developer changes the start of a dialog, switches the model, or updates account data, the system automatically resets the saved reasoning context.
This can make responses less accurate and increase token costs because the model will have to analyze everything again.
To avoid this and keep the cache working, it is recommended not to touch the start of the dialog.
In addition, the API has changed the order in which instructions are passed.

The reusable system rules now advise writing to the first message with the developer role inside the input block so that they are cached, and leaving the top-level instructions field only for one-time tasks.
Also, the new models no longer support Flex mode — instead, a cheaper background mode has appeared for long tasks that can run for two or eight hours.
The OpenAI Docs skill tool, paired with an AI agent, can help quickly update old code to meet new requirements.

Recall that despite high performance in internal tests and a 20% reduction in the cost of the flagship via API, the release of GPT 6.2 was accompanied by a wave of criticism from well-known developers, investors, and researchers who tested the models before launch.
